title: Mountaineering records
intro: First ascents and climbing records capture particular moments in a changing sport. Definitions matter: route, season, summit verification, use of oxygen and the record-keeping body can affect a claim. Always check the linked source for the latest status.
heroAlt: Mount Everest rising above the Himalaya

sections.heading: The fourteen 8,000-metre peaks
sections.text: The fourteen conventionally recognized mountains above 8,000 metres span the Himalaya and Karakoram. Their first ascents were achieved by international teams over several decades. These records should recognize the expedition members and local high-altitude workers who contributed to each climb.
sections.alt: Mount Everest, one of the fourteen conventionally recognized 8,000-metre peaks
facts: There are fourteen conventionally recognized 8,000-metre peaks.
Peak heights may vary slightly among maps and surveying sources.

sections.heading: First ascents and changing milestones
sections.text: The first ascent of a summit is only one kind of achievement. Later milestones include winter ascents, routes without supplemental oxygen, solo climbs and faster completions. Many record claims are time-sensitive and depend on independently checking the route and summit details.

modules.heading: Notable first ascents and records
modules.asOf: As of 12 October 2026. The Himalayan Database coverage reviewed here runs through Autumn–Winter 2025. Records are category- and source-dependent; check the linked record keeper for later updates.
modules.note: Historical age and speed milestones below are date-stamped achievements, not a guarantee that they remain the current world record. Speed claims are especially sensitive to definitions and subsequent updates.
